_meta.scope: Faithful structural reading of the SOURCE (Lewis Carroll, Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, ch001-ch012). No adaptation decisions are taken here; points where the realistic premise (brief.md) will need a later ruling are listed in realism_notes only.
_meta.citation_convention: chapter = chNNN (story/chapter_manifest.json); scene = chNNN-scNN; paras = chNNN-pNN (structured_story paragraph ids). Ranges are [first, last] inclusive.
_meta.event_refs_policy: Every node carries event_refs with ids from story/events.json (ev0001-ev0054), back-filled at the G1 cross-check (task p1-structure-eventrefs). Mapping rule: an event is referenced when its source paragraph range (events.json 'source') overlaps the paragraphs the node cites; acts reference every event in their chapter span; arcs reference the union of their beats; foreshadowing carries setup_ref.event_refs / payoff_ref.event_refs / via[].event_refs plus their union at node level; edges carry the events that realise the link. No ev* id outside events.json is used.

revisions.change: event_refs back-filled from story/events.json (placement cross-checked with story/story_timeline.json); open_questions_for_g1 statused. No node id, chapter/scene/paragraph citation or structural judgement changed.

edge_types.causal: the source node makes the target happen (plot necessity)
edge_types.echo: the target deliberately mirrors / rhymes with the source (thematic, no plot necessity)
edge_types.setup_payoff: shorthand edge generated by a foreshadowing entry
edge_types.enables: the source gives the protagonist a capability used at the target

summary.logline: A bored girl follows a hurrying White Rabbit underground, spends one afternoon trying to reach a glimpsed garden while her body and her sense of self keep changing, finds the garden ruled by an arbitrary Queen, and wakes on the riverbank the moment she stops deferring to the court.
summary.shape: Episodic picaresque with a single goal thread (reach the garden) and a single inner thread (who am I / whose authority counts). Chapters 1-7 are a quest for the garden; chapters 8-12 are the garden's court world, which escalates from game (croquet) to law (trial). A realistic frame (the bank, the sister) opens ch001 and closes ch012.
summary.narrative_engine: Each chapter = one new host/rule-set that tests Alice (size, manners, logic, authority). Progress is measured by (a) size control and (b) how far Alice will contradict an adult/authority figure.

coda.note: Point of view hands over to the sister, who re-maps each Wonderland sound onto a real farmyard sound (ch012-p70).

acts.name: The Descent and the Locked Garden
acts.function: Setup: ordinary world (bank, sister, boredom), call (White Rabbit with watch), threshold (rabbit-hole), the concrete goal (the little door and the garden) and the core obstacle (wrong size). Ends with Alice literally swimming in the consequence of her own tears.

evidence.note: book without pictures or conversations — the boredom that motivates the whole adventure
garden glimpsed through the little door: goal fixed
'Who in the world am I?' — inner question fixed
falls into the pool of tears — act-closing reversal

acts.name: Wandering Outside the Garden: Learning the Rules
acts.function: Fun-and-games half of the confrontation: a succession of hosts (Dodo/Mouse, White Rabbit's household, Caterpillar, Pigeon, Duchess, Cheshire Cat) each imposing a rule-set; Alice is ordered about, loses her identity repeatedly, but gains the one real tool of the book — controlled size via the mushroom — and the explicit plan (right size, then garden).

evidence.note: 'we're all mad here' — thesis of the world stated

acts.name: Inside the Garden: The Court of Hearts
acts.function: Midpoint victory (Alice finally enters the garden, ch007-sc03) turns sour: the garden is a regime of executions, rigged croquet and card-people. Alice begins to talk back ('Nonsense!'), learns the threats are hollow (Gryphon), and is given a pause of melancholy reflection (Mock Turtle) before being summoned to the trial.

acts.name: The Trial and the Waking
acts.function: Climax: the court gathers most of the book's cast; Alice grows without any food or drink, is called as a witness, openly defies the Queen and dissolves the whole world by naming it ('nothing but a pack of cards'). Resolution: waking on the bank; coda from the sister's point of view.

evidence.note: Alice begins to grow in court, unprompted

structure_points.desc: A White Rabbit runs past saying 'I shall be late!' and takes a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket — the first impossible detail, noticed only in retrospect.
Alice follows it down the rabbit-hole 'never once considering how in the world she was to get out again'.
The hall of locked doors, the golden key, the little door and 'the loveliest garden you ever saw': the goal that organises the next six chapters.
Giant, weeping, key in hand but still unable to pass; identity crisis ('Who in the world am I?') and the fall into her own pool of tears.
After escaping the Rabbit's house Alice formulates the plan: first grow to my right size, second find the way into that lovely garden.
Caterpillar: 'One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter.' First time a rule of this world is usable; mastered at ch005-p77.
Cheshire Cat: 'we're all mad here. I'm mad. You're mad.' The world's governing claim, which Alice will finally reject in ch012.
False victory: using key + mushroom Alice at last walks into the garden (goal of act 1 achieved) — and the garden turns out to be the Queen's domain.
'they're only a pack of cards … I needn't be afraid of them' and 'Nonsense!' silences the Queen: the first time Alice openly overrules an authority.
The croquet game: 'Off with his head!' once a minute; Alice fears for her own head ('the great wonder is, that there's any one left alive').

The game ends with every player except King, Queen and Alice under sentence; Alice is the last one standing in a world that removes people. Immediately softened by the King's whispered pardon (ch009-p42) and the Gryphon's reveal (ch009-p46).
By the sea Alice retells her own adventures and concludes she was 'a different person' yesterday — the book's quiet self-assessment before the climax.
'The trial's beginning!' — the Gryphon drags Alice off; all threads converge on the court.
Alice begins to grow larger with no food or drink — her size now tracks her confidence, not the world's rules.
The White Rabbit calls the next witness: 'Alice!' (chapter cliffhanger).
'Sentence first—verdict afterwards.' / 'Stuff and nonsense!' / 'Off with her head!' Nobody moved. / 'Who cares for you? You're nothing but a pack of cards!' — the pack flies up at her.
Alice wakes on the bank with her head in her sister's lap; tells the dream; is sent in to tea.
The sister half-dreams Wonderland, maps each marvel onto 'dull reality', and imagines grown-up Alice telling the tale to children.

arcs.label: External goal: reach the garden
arcs.contribution: The book's only sustained plot goal; gives chapters 1-7 direction and turns chapters 8-12 into 'what the garden really is'.

beats.desc: Glimpses the garden; too big for the door.
Shrinks to ten inches but has left the key on the table — first failure caused by poor sequencing.
Nine feet high with the key; shrinks again; door shut, key back on the table: 'things are worse than ever'.
Plan articulated: right size first, then the garden.
Masters size with the two mushroom pieces.
Returns to the long hall, key first, then mushroom: 'I'll manage better this time' — enters the garden (midpoint).
The garden's first image: gardeners painting white roses red to avoid beheading — the dream garden is a place of fear.
Rejects the garden's rulers outright; the goal is transcended rather than kept.

arcs.label: Inner arc: 'Who in the world am I?' → self-possession
arcs.contribution: The thematic spine; every host asks Alice what she is, and each answer is less borrowed than the last.

beats.desc: Established trait: 'very fond of pretending to be two people' — she scolds and advises herself.
Wonders if she has been changed for Ada or Mabel; lessons fail; resolves to stay down if she is Mabel.
First recitation comes out wrong ('How doth the little crocodile').
Mistaken for the housemaid Mary Ann and obeys at once — identity assigned by others.
Caterpillar: 'Who are you?' — she cannot answer: 'I must have been changed several times since then.'
Pigeon calls her a serpent; 'I'm a—I'm a—' she cannot finish; the Pigeon: 'what does it matter to me whether you're a little girl or a serpent?'
Cheshire Cat assigns her madness: 'You're mad … or you wouldn't have come here.'
Owns the change: 'it's no use going back to yesterday, because I was a different person then.'
'I won't!' / 'Who cares for you?' — defines herself against the court instead of by it.
The sister's projection: Alice will keep 'the simple and loving heart of her childhood' into adulthood — the arc's endpoint seen from outside.

arcs.label: Social arc: deference → defiance
arcs.contribution: Measures growth in behaviour: from running errands for a rabbit to silencing a queen. The climax is the terminus of this arc, not of the garden arc.

beats.desc: Argues with the Lory, who wins by seniority: 'I am older than you, and must know better.'
Ordered by the Rabbit to fetch gloves and a fan; runs off 'so much frightened'.
'being ordered about by mice and rabbits' — names the grievance for the first time.
Swallows her temper when the Caterpillar says 'Keep your temper'.
'Nobody asked your opinion'; finally walks out of the tea-party in disgust — first exit on her own terms.
'How should I know? It's no business of mine.' then 'Nonsense!' — the Queen falls silent.
'Stuff and nonsense!' 'I won't!' 'Who cares for you?' — full defiance at full size.

arcs.label: Mechanic arc: involuntary size change → mastered → size = self
arcs.contribution: Externalises the identity arc: every size change is an identity wobble; mastery (ch005) enables the midpoint; unprompted growth in court (ch011-ch012) makes the climax physically possible.

beats.desc: 'DRINK ME': shuts up like a telescope to ten inches.
'EAT ME' cake.
Grows past nine feet ('Curiouser and curiouser!'), then shrinks via the Rabbit's fan, nearly to nothing.
Unlabelled bottle: fills the Rabbit's house.
Pebbles thrown in turn to cakes; one shrinks her and she escapes (escape runs into ch004-sc04).
First mushroom test: chin strikes foot.
Serpent neck above the trees; then careful alternation brings her to usual height — mastery.
Chooses nine inches so as not to frighten the Duchess's household — first deliberate size choice.
Raises herself to two feet before the March Hare's house.
Pocket mushroom → one foot high → through the door.
Begins to grow in court without eating anything; decides to stay 'as long as there was room for her'.
Tips over the jury-box; Rule Forty-two aimed at her; 'grown to her full size' at the climax.

arcs.label: Frame: the bank, the sister, the dream
arcs.contribution: Bookends the fantasy with the realistic world; the only place where the source itself offers a 'reality' reading of the marvels (ch012-p70). Critical anchor for the realistic premise.

beats.desc: Hot day, sleepy and stupid, sister's book without pictures or conversations.
Wakes; dead leaves on her face (= the flying cards); 'a curious dream'; sent to tea — 'it's getting late' (echo of the Rabbit).
Sister's reverie and projection of Alice's future.

arcs.label: The White Rabbit: late for the Duchess → herald of the court
arcs.contribution: The guide/lure figure: pulls Alice in (ch001), drops the fan that shrinks her (ch002), commands her (ch004), explains the Duchess's peril (ch008), and calls her to the witness stand (ch011). His anxiety introduces the Queen's terror long before the Queen appears.

beats.desc: 'I shall be late!' with watch.
'Oh my ears and whiskers, how late it's getting!' — vanishes in the hall.
Dressed up, gloves and fan: 'Oh! the Duchess, the Duchess! … if I've kept her waiting!' — drops them fleeing Alice.
'She'll get me executed' — orders 'Mary Ann' home for gloves and fan.
Besieges his own house with Pat and Bill; threatens to burn it down.
Whispers why: the Duchess is under sentence for boxing the Queen's ears.
Herald: reads the accusation.
Calls 'Alice!'.
Corrects the King ('Unimportant'); reads the verses.

arcs.label: The pool creatures and the Mouse's grudge
arcs.contribution: First society Alice meets; establishes the pattern that Alice's home talk (Dinah) alienates Wonderland's inhabitants, leaving her alone at the end of ch003.

beats.desc: Alice offends the Mouse with Dinah; Mouse promises its history 'why it is I hate cats and dogs'.
The driest lesson; the Caucus-race where everybody wins; Alice gives comfits and receives her own thimble.
'Mine is a long and a sad tale!' — Alice mishears 'tale'/'tail' and 'not'/'knot'; the Mouse leaves insulted.
Mentioning Dinah again empties the bank.
Alone and crying; pattering footsteps (hand-off to the Rabbit).

arcs.label: Bill the Lizard: chimney victim → juror
arcs.contribution: A minor comic thread that silently ties act 2a to the trial and gives Alice two involuntary acts of harm to the same small creature (the kick up the chimney; putting him head-down in the jury-box).

beats.desc: Sent down the chimney; Alice kicks him out; 'up I goes like a sky-rocket'.
Revived by two guinea-pigs.
Juror; Alice takes his squeaking pencil; he writes with his finger.
Replaced head-downwards; later uses the ink trickling from the inkstand the Queen throws.

arcs.label: The Duchess, her cook, the baby and the Cheshire Cat
arcs.contribution: Bridges the outer world to the court: the croquet invitation (ch006) is the first link to the Queen; the Duchess's sentence (ch008) and reprieve/flight (ch009) show the Queen's power; the cook reappears as a witness (ch011). Tonal study: violent kitchen → saccharine moralising Duchess (Alice's pepper theory).

beats.desc: Fish-Footman delivers 'An invitation from the Queen to play croquet.'
Pepper-filled kitchen; cook throws crockery; 'chop off her head!'; Duchess flings the baby to Alice and leaves for croquet.
The baby turns into a pig and trots into the wood.
Revealed: the Duchess boxed the Queen's ears and is under sentence of execution.
Alice: the Cat 'belongs to the Duchess' — the Duchess is fetched out of prison.
Affectionate, moral-quoting Duchess; Alice's theory that pepper makes people hot-tempered.
'either you or your head must be off' — the Duchess flees.
The cook testifies ('Pepper, mostly') and disappears in the confusion.

arcs.event_refs_note: ev0025 (Alice and the Frog-Footman at the door, ch006-p05-p18) is the thread's connective tissue between the invitation beat and the kitchen beat; it has no beat of its own because it carries no structural turn.

arcs.label: The Cheshire Cat: guide who cannot be governed
arcs.contribution: The only inhabitant who is friendly to Alice and immune to the Queen; gives directions (Hatter/March Hare), states the thesis of the world, and at croquet exposes the limits of the Queen's power (a head with no body cannot be cut off).

beats.desc: Grinning on the Duchess's hearth.
'if you only walk long enough'; directions to the Hatter and the March Hare; 'we're all mad here'.
'You'll see me there' (croquet); asks after the baby; vanishes leaving the grin.
Grin appears at croquet; Alice introduces 'a friend of mine' to the King.
Executioner/King/Queen dispute over beheading a bodiless head; the head fades.

arcs.label: Hatter, March Hare, Dormouse: the stopped clock
arcs.contribution: Plants the Queen's tyranny by report (the concert, 'murdering the time', ch007-p55) before the Queen is seen; pays off in the trial where the Queen recognises the Hatter and terrorises him.

beats.desc: 'Your hair wants cutting'; 'Why is a raven like a writing-desk?'
Quarrel with Time at the Queen's concert; 'He's murdering the time! Off with his head!'; ever since it is always six o'clock, always tea-time.
Dormouse's treacle-well tale, repeatedly interrupted.
Alice leaves; they try to put the Dormouse into the teapot.
First witness with teacup and bread-and-butter ('hadn't quite finished my tea'); 'It isn't mine' (hat); the Queen stares and demands the list of singers at the last concert; he shakes off his shoes.
'I'm a poor man, your Majesty'; leaves the court without his shoes.
Dormouse answers 'Treacle' out of turn and is turned out of court.

arcs.label: The Queen of Hearts: threat by report → threat in person → exposed as empty
arcs.contribution: The antagonist force. Built by hearsay for six chapters (Rabbit, Duchess, Hatter), embodied in ch008-ch009, revealed as hollow by the Gryphon (ch009) and the King's pardons, and finally defied into nothing at the climax.

beats.desc: By report (via the Duchess): 'She'll get me executed'.
Invitation to croquet — the Queen's first named appearance.
By report: 'Off with his head!' at the concert.
The procession; 'Off with her head!' at Alice — silenced by 'Nonsense!'.
Croquet: a sentence 'about once in a minute'.
All players in custody; the King's whispered 'You are all pardoned'.
Gryphon: 'It's all her fancy, that: they never executes nobody.'
'Sentence first—verdict afterwards.' 'Off with her head!' — Nobody moved.

arcs.label: The Knave of Hearts and the stolen tarts
arcs.contribution: Supplies the climax's pretext. The Knave is planted silently in the procession; the trial's 'evidence' is absurd, the tarts are on the table all along, and no verdict is ever reached — the legal plot is deliberately left open so Alice's defiance, not a verdict, ends it.

beats.desc: Carries the King's crown on a cushion; bows and smiles when the Queen asks who Alice is; turns the gardeners over with one foot.
In chains; dish of tarts on the table; accusation read as the nursery rhyme.
'Consider your verdict' — before any evidence.
Unsigned verses produced; Knave: 'there's no name signed at the end'.
King 'decodes' the verses; 'Why, there they are!' pointing at the tarts on the table.
'Sentence first—verdict afterwards.' — trial collapses with no verdict.

arcs.label: The Mock Turtle and the Gryphon: lost schooldays by the sea
arcs.contribution: The breather before the climax: nostalgia, parodied schooling and dance; mirrors Alice's own failed lessons; the Gryphon delivers the key information that the executions are empty and escorts Alice to the trial.

beats.desc: The Queen: 'Have you seen the Mock Turtle yet?' — 'the thing Mock Turtle Soup is made from'.
Gryphon wakes; 'they never executes nobody'.
'Once I was a real Turtle'; school under the sea (Reeling and Writhing, the Classics master).
The Lobster Quadrille danced round Alice; whiting 'does the boots and shoes'.
Alice tells her own adventures; recites 'Tis the voice of the Lobster' wrong.
'Beautiful Soup' cut off by 'The trial's beginning!'; the Mock Turtle left singing behind.

arcs.label: Caterpillar and Pigeon: the identity examiners
arcs.contribution: Self-contained episode that delivers both the practical tool (mushroom) and the sharpest statement of the identity question; no later return (see fs-caterpillar-used-to-it for the one hanging thread).

beats.desc: Mushroom found with the Caterpillar on top.
'Who are you?'; 'Father William' recited wrong.
'You'll get used to it in time'; the mushroom rule.
Pigeon: 'Serpent!'; Alice's truthful admission that she eats eggs.

intersections.desc: The garden quest and the size mechanic resolve together: the lesson of ch001 (take the key first) plus the tool of ch005.
First convergence: Rabbit, Knave, King and Queen share one scene; Alice's first 'Nonsense!'.
The Cat's beheading dispute brings the Duchess out of prison into ch009.
Grand convergence: the court collects characters from acts 1, 2a and 2b.
Witness sequence re-runs the tea-party and the kitchen under the Queen's eye while Alice grows.
All three Alice arcs terminate on the same line: full size + defiance + self-definition.
The flying cards become dead leaves; the frame reclaims the story.

foreshadowing.label: 'I shall be late' — lateness for the Duchess
foreshadowing.note: The reason for the Rabbit's panic is only explained in ch008: the Duchess is under sentence and the Queen had been kept waiting. Final echo ch012-p66 'it's getting late'.

foreshadowing.label: Golden key + little door + garden
foreshadowing.note: Double failure (ch001-p23, ch002-p15) sets up the 'I'll manage better this time' payoff.

foreshadowing.label: Alice's plan: right size, then the garden
Mushroom rule ('one side … the other side')
foreshadowing.note: The piece 'kept in her pocket' is the explicit bridge.

foreshadowing.label: Rabbit's fan and gloves
foreshadowing.note: Dropped items cause both the shrinking (fan, ch002-p14) and the Mary Ann errand (ch004). See fs-006 for the errand's own open end.

foreshadowing.label: Errand never completed: Alice never delivers fan and gloves
foreshadowing.note: Alice picks up a fan and gloves in the Rabbit's room, drinks from the bottle, and the objects are never mentioned again; the Rabbit is next seen fully dressed in the procession (ch008-sc02). Adaptation must decide whether to close or drop it.

foreshadowing.label: Mary Ann (the Rabbit's housemaid)
foreshadowing.note: Alice fears meeting 'the real Mary Ann' (ch004-p03); she never appears.

foreshadowing.label: Dinah the cat
foreshadowing.note: Recurring token of home (her saucer of milk 'at tea-time') that repeatedly alienates Wonderland creatures; Dinah never appears, not even at the waking in ch012. Thematic cousin: the Cheshire Cat (the only cat in Wonderland) — echo, not payoff.

foreshadowing.label: Mouse's history: why it hates cats and dogs
foreshadowing.note: Delivered as the 'long and sad tale' (shape poem, a dog named Fury); Alice mishears and the Mouse walks off — partial payoff: the tale is told but the relationship is not repaired.

foreshadowing.label: Queen's croquet invitation
Cheshire Cat: 'You'll see me there'
The grin without a cat
foreshadowing.note: The vanishing trick established in ch006 is what defeats the executioner in ch008.

foreshadowing.label: Directions: a Hatter one way, a March Hare the other — 'both mad'
Hatter's quarrel with Time at the Queen's concert
foreshadowing.note: The Queen recognises him and demands 'the list of singers in the last concert'.

foreshadowing.label: Always six o'clock / always tea-time
foreshadowing.note: The Hatter arrives at court with teacup and bread-and-butter: 'I hadn't quite finished my tea when I was sent for.'

foreshadowing.label: Hatter's riddle: 'Why is a raven like a writing-desk?'
foreshadowing.note: Explicitly unanswerable in the source (Alice: 'riddles that have no answers', ch007-p38). Must stay flagged; any adaptation that answers it is inventing.

foreshadowing.label: Dormouse's treacle-well story
foreshadowing.note: Never finished — Alice leaves mid-tale. Faint echo in court: the Dormouse's 'Treacle' (ch011-p70), which is an echo, not a completion.

foreshadowing.label: Dormouse to be put in the teapot
foreshadowing.note: Structural rhyme: stuffed into a teapot / stuffed into a canvas bag and turned out of court.

foreshadowing.label: Too much pepper; the cook
Duchess 'under sentence' for boxing the Queen's ears
foreshadowing.note: Duchess fetched from prison (ch008-p71), then chased off ('either you or your head'). Her ultimate fate is not stated; she survives by fleeing.

foreshadowing.label: The Cheshire Cat's fate after the beheading dispute
foreshadowing.note: The head fades while the King and executioner run about; the dispute is never decided and the Cat never returns (not even at the trial). The Cat is also absent from the sister's reverie (ch012-p68-p70).

foreshadowing.label: 'Off with his head!' — are the executions real?
foreshadowing.note: Payoff defuses Alice's (and the audience's) fear and licenses her full defiance at ch012-p62 ('Nobody moved').

foreshadowing.label: Card people: 'only a pack of cards, after all'
foreshadowing.note: The thought whispered in ch008 becomes the world-ending line spoken aloud in ch012. Strongest single setup/payoff in the book.

foreshadowing.label: The Knave in the procession
Did the Knave steal the tarts? (verdict)
foreshadowing.note: No verdict is ever returned; the tarts are on the court table (ch011-p01, ch012-p54); the trial dissolves at ch012-p63. Deliberately open in the source.

foreshadowing.label: Author of the unsigned verses
foreshadowing.note: The King treats the missing signature as proof of guilt; authorship is never established.

foreshadowing.label: Bill the Lizard
The two guinea-pigs
foreshadowing.note: Two guinea-pigs cheer in court and are 'suppressed' (ch011-p53, ch011-p58; echoed in ch012-p69). Identity with the ch004 pair is implied, not stated.

foreshadowing.label: 'When I grow up, I'll write one' (a book about this)
foreshadowing.note: Paid off indirectly by the sister's vision of grown Alice telling 'the dream of Wonderland' to children; also meta-payoff of 'a book without pictures or conversations' (ch001-p01).

foreshadowing.label: 'Who in the world am I?'
foreshadowing.note: Never answered in words; answered in action at the climax.

foreshadowing.label: Growing in court without a trigger
Sleepy on the bank / the dream frame
foreshadowing.note: Source withholds the dream reading until the end; ch012-p70 then maps sounds to reality.

foreshadowing.label: Caterpillar: 'You'll get used to it in time'
foreshadowing.note: Paid off locally: 'it felt quite strange at first; but she got used to it in a few minutes'.

foreshadowing.label: Baby that becomes a pig
foreshadowing.note: The pig-baby resurfaces only in the sister's reverie (ch012-p69).

foreshadowing.label: Mock Turtle introduced by the Queen
'The trial's beginning!'
Mock Turtle's 'Beautiful Soup' left unfinished
foreshadowing.note: Gryphon leaves 'without waiting for the end of the song'; the Mock Turtle and Gryphon are not shown again apart from the sister's reverie (ch012-p69, p70). Whether the Gryphon remains at Alice's side during the trial after ch011-sc01 is not stated.

foreshadowing.label: Alice's sister and her book

motifs.label: Lessons and poems come out wrong
motifs.function: Measures the loss of Alice's borrowed (schoolroom) identity; mirrored by the Mock Turtle's parody curriculum (ch009-sc05).

motifs.label: Labelled food/drink as a test

occurrences.desc: tarts that make Alice hungry — the one food she never touches

motifs.function: Temptation → consequence; inverted at the trial where the food is the evidence.

motifs.label: Time, lateness and tea

occurrences.desc: 'run in to your tea; it's getting late'

motifs.function: The Rabbit's watch, the stopped six o'clock, and the real tea-time bracket the dream in clock time.

motifs.label: 'Off with his/her head!'
motifs.function: Escalating threat that is emptied by ch009-p46 and fails outright at ch012-p62.

motifs.label: Madness as the world's norm
motifs.function: Stated thesis the ending refutes by re-framing as dream/reality.

motifs.label: 'Curious' / 'Curiouser and curiouser'
motifs.function: Alice's verbal signature; closes the book.

motifs.label: Alice alone, crying, then resolving
motifs.function: Act-1 emotional pattern; disappears after ch005 as her competence grows (arc evidence).

edges.note: the tears make the pool; the pool makes the creature society
dropped fan and gloves lead to the Mary Ann errand and the Rabbit's house
escape from the Rabbit's house → the wood → the mushroom
the invitation is the first concrete link from the wood to the Queen
leaving the tea-party leads to the tree door into the hall
the Queen sends Alice to the Mock Turtle
knowing the threats are empty licenses defiance
'Who in the world am I?' → 'I was a different person then'
Alice's broken lessons ↔ the Mock Turtle's parody school

natural_cliffhangers.desc: chapter ends on the EAT ME cake — size outcome pending (ch001-p30 is a section divider)
eyes meet the Caterpillar on the mushroom
the little house in the clearing

self_contained_units.desc: pool of tears + Caucus-race + Mouse's tale

episode_planner_hints.load_bearing_chain: sp-opening-hook → sp-inciting-incident → sp-first-plot-point → sp-plan-stated → sp-tool-acquired → sp-midpoint → sp-first-defiance → fs-022 payoff (ch009-p46) → sp-second-plot-point → sp-climax-setup → sp-climax → sp-resolution. Events on this chain should not be cut.

realism_notes.status: flags_only — no decision taken here; to be ruled by 02-worldbuilding/magic-cultivation + world (SUP-* entries) and confirmed at H1 (bible/WRITE_RULES.md §7.1).
realism_notes.event_refs_note: Aligned with story/events.json realistic_adaptation_flags (aspects: dream frame; talking animals and living-card figures; physical size changes; objects transforming; impossible geography).
